# Contextual after-spacing across cells

These are original, manually authored OOXML controls generated by
`tools/cell_next_context_fixture.py`. The generator reuses only the original OPC
skeleton from the cell-end-context fixture and replaces its document and styles.
No template content or third-party engine is included.

The reference application exported `control-native.pdf` using the repository's owned automation
reference helper. `tools/record_cell_next_context.py` records native glyph origins
and source/PDF hashes. `cases.json` describes all 48 pages: Normal/custom current
style, same-row/next-row boundary, empty/nonempty final paragraph, three following
styles, and contextual spacing on/off. Each tested final paragraph stores 8 pt
of after-spacing. Arial must be installed for native comparisons.

Within a row, the reference application suppresses that after-spacing only when contextual spacing is
on and the next cell's first paragraph has the same style. At a row boundary,
the reference application retains the previously established implicit Normal-style context, regardless
of the next row's actual style. Empty and nonempty paragraphs behave alike.
Before the correction, custom same-style cells retained unwanted spacing, and
Normal cells incorrectly lost spacing before differently styled cells.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.1.9 and 17.3.1.33 describe contextual suppression
and paragraph spacing. The clause does not explicitly define paragraph adjacency
across cells or the implicit row-end paragraph. These observed boundary semantics
are supported as observed compatibility behavior, without template exceptions.

Unit coverage checks all row heights, the compatibility override, changing the
next cell's paragraph style, reopening, unrelated package parts and exact undo.
Browser coverage checks all native text origins within 0.2 pt, page count,
editing, export and reopening. Existing cell-end and row/merge controls run
alongside these controls.
